articles.title: Arman Tsarukyan Has ONE Goal: Become UFC Champion #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan has one goal—and he isn’t letting anything distract him from it: becoming UFC champion. Chael Sonnen reveals his conversation with Arman about preparing for five rounds, staying active in wrestling and jiu-jitsu, and balancing those competitions with his MMA training. Arman’s answer was simple: no matter how big another match is, he never stops training MMA. That mindset is what makes Tsarukyan different. Wrestling and jiu-jitsu aren’t competing with his MMA career—they’re part of the preparation for it. Arman isn’t focused on collecting accomplishments outside the UFC. He wants the UFC lightweight championship, and everything he does is ultimately pointed toward that goal. Chael breaks down why that kind of singular focus can separate an elite fighter from everyone else. #UFC #MMA #ArmanTsarukyan #ChaelSonnen #UFCChampion #UFCNews #UFCTraining #Wrestling #JiuJitsu

articles.title: Jon Jones Could Be Coming Back for the Belt #ufc
articles.description: Jon Jones’ path back to the UFC heavyweight title may have just changed completely. With Tom Aspinall no longer standing in the way, Chael Sonnen examines what could be next for Jones if he decides to return. Dana White has repeatedly indicated that a returning Jon Jones would go straight into a world title fight — but which division, and against whom? articles.title: This Is Why I Love Wrestling
articles.description: Sometimes in wrestling, you only need one good day. Chael Sonnen tells the story of Blaine Natal, a wrestler he's known and coached for years. Blaine has spent his life showing up, taking the hard matches and refusing to let failure determine whether he steps on the mat again. His mother, Candy, has been there for all of it. But for all the years of work, Blaine was still waiting for that day. Then he drew Noah Wachsmuth, an undefeated Oregon champion and former Olympic Training Center athlete. On paper, this wasn't supposed to be Blaine's moment. For much of the match, it didn't look like it would be. But wrestling doesn't reward how impressive something looks. The scoreboard does the talking. When time expired, Blaine had one more point. After 22 years, he finally had his day. For Chael, it was one of those rare moments in sports that brought a tear to his eye. You don't need 10 years of perfect days. Sometimes you just need one. articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into two hundred in total bonuses, paid over 21 days. The Crown Is Yours! A lot of fans aren't simply saying they'd rather see another matchup. They're arguing that there is no competitive reason to run this fight back. Chael couldn't disagree more. Topuria hurt Gaethje badly, pushed for the finish, and ultimately faded as the fight went long. Sean O'Malley even pointed out a moment where Topuria may have been able to secure a TKO had he walked away after dropping Gaethje with a body shot. Then look at Topuria's résumé. He was undefeated, a two-division UFC champion, stopped Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira, and entered the Gaethje fight after a long period of inactivity and major changes outside the cage. So why is a rematch suddenly unreasonable? Chael breaks down the competitive case for Topuria vs Gaethje 2, responds to Luke Thomas' argument, and explains why this fight may have far more justification than people are giving it credit for. Would you run Topuria vs Gaethje back, or should both men move on? articles.title: Is Tommy McMillen the UFC’s Next Superstar?
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into two hundred in total bonuses, paid over 21 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner Could Tommy “Gun” McMillen become the second-biggest star in UFC history? Conor McGregor remains the standard, but determining who belongs directly behind him is more complicated. Georges St-Pierre produced enormous pay-per-view numbers. Paddy Pimblett has become a massive attraction. Ilia Topuria, Islam Makhachev, Sean O’Malley, Ronda Rousey and Jon Jones all have arguments depending on how stardom is measured. Chael Sonnen believes McMillen could eventually surpass nearly all of them. Tommy has the fighting ability, an authentic personality and the rare ability to deliver a promotional line without making it sound rehearsed. He also trains alongside O’Malley under Tim Welch, giving him access to people who understand that becoming a star requires more than winning fights. McMillen’s undefeated record survived another major test at Noche UFC when he defeated Marwan Rahiki by unanimous decision in a back-and-forth fight. Instead of exposing Tommy, the adversity allowed him to demonstrate toughness, composure and the ability to close strongly. There are still questions. Tommy must continue winning, reach numbered UFC events and discover what will motivate him once the money and attention arrive. But right now, Chael sees no evidence that disqualifies him from becoming the UFC’s next transcendent superstar. But this story may be more complicated than it first appears. After Gane’s disappointing loss to Jon Jones, another opportunity to become undisputed champion appeared almost impossible. The UFC had no interest in booking that rematch. Somehow, Gane worked his way back, defeated Alex Pereira for the interim title and now stands as the undisputed heavyweight champion. Chael Sonnen explains why Gane’s career looks completely different today. His close fight with Francis Ngannou carries more weight, his championship résumé continues to grow and the dangerous fighter who emerged from the White House event may be better than anyone realized. Tom’s departure also creates another possibility: could Jon Jones come back? Jones never seemed interested in facing Aspinall. But would he return for a championship fight against an opponent he has already defeated? Chael examines whether Gane’s rise could reopen the door for Jones, what that would mean for Josh Hokit and why another Jon Jones title reign could create even more problems for the heavyweight division. Is Ciryl Gane the biggest winner from Tom Aspinall vacating, or does this situation benefit Jon Jones even more?
